fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeNiMn-Cu system is unrelated to the target CrFeTaVW/CrFeTiVW refractory HEAs and does not reconstruct the Ta-to-Ti substitution.
Neither cited source supports Cu-rich grain-boundary channels, their percolation at approximately 5 at.% Cu, or improved thermal transport in the proposed alloy.
The assumed coherent, stable, percolating grain-boundary Cu network is internally questionable and is presented without thermodynamic, kinetic, or microstructural evidence.
The predicted conductivity improvement conflicts with the target result that Ta-to-Ti substitution changed phase constitution but had little effect on thermal diffusivity.
explanation: The response addresses the broad engineering objective and proposes a composition-controlled comparison with a falsification threshold, but it is not a reconstruction of the target study. It changes both the alloy family and intervention, omits the mechanical-alloying/SPS and hybrid MD/MC framework, and invokes a transport mechanism absent from the target. Its temperature range only partly overlaps the target measurements, while loading and plasma-facing claims are not substantiated. The control alloy and combined thermal/microstructural/mechanical measurements provide some discriminability, but thin-film laser-flash testing and nanoindentation are not sufficient demonstrations of bulk intermediate-layer thermal conductivity and creep integrity. The cited phase-prediction and generic creep studies do not validate the central Cu-channel hypothesis.
